answer_1.quote: We propose KB-BINDER, which, for the first time, enables training-free few-shot in-context learning on KBQA. ... In the first stage, we demonstrate a few KBQA questions and their corresponding logical forms as the exemplary pairs for Codex to generate a draft of an unseen question. The draft is a 'preliminary' logical form ... We fill the bound entities and relations into the draft to generate a set of 'refined' logical forms. We execute these logical forms against the KB and return the executed results as the answer.
answer_1.outputs: preliminary logical form drafts and refined executable logical forms (e.g., SPARQL queries)

answer_2.quote: We evaluate our pipeline on all the test sets ... We compare our method with all the systems that have a publication on the official leaderboard of each dataset and record their results ... The evaluation metrics reported include EM, F1, and Hits@1 scores.
